candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — prevention, screening and anticipatory guidance
candidate.educational_objective: Apply the cited evidence to recognize the uniquely safest or most accurate nursing response in the clinical situation tested by V2-Q0147.

options.A: Screening should begin now because the USPSTF recommends colorectal cancer screening for average-risk adults ages 45 to 49 as a Grade B service.
options.B: Screening should wait until age 50 because the USPSTF gives no recommendation for asymptomatic average-risk adults before age 50 unless symptoms appear.
options.C: Screening is recommended only after age 75 because earlier testing has no net benefit for asymptomatic adults who do not have a family history.
options.D: Screening should begin before age 50 only when a first-degree relative had colorectal cancer, because age alone does not support screening at 47.

candidate.rationale: The USPSTF final recommendation gives a Grade B recommendation to screen average-risk adults ages 45 to 49 for colorectal cancer and Grade A for ages 50 to 75. It applies to asymptomatic adults at average risk, so an average-risk 47-year-old should not wait solely because age 50 has not been reached.
candidate.source_claim_supported: USPSTF recommends colorectal cancer screening for average-risk adults ages 45–49 (Grade B), including asymptomatic adults at average risk.
candidate.source_locator: USPSTF Final Recommendation Statement (May 18, 2021) — Recommendation Summary / Patient Population: ages 45–49 Grade B; asymptomatic average-risk adults
candidate.source_version_date: USPSTF Final Recommendation Statement 2021-05-18; current published recommendation rechecked 2026-08-16
candidate.stem: An asymptomatic, average-risk 47-year-old adult asks whether colorectal cancer screening can wait until age 50. Which response best reflects the current USPSTF recommendation?
